name: native-goal-function-interface-results-sept24
result: The JSON-schema/native-function interface change failed with Qwen and with the smaller LFM model. Both Qwen outputs marked the explicit supplied URL unsupported; its function output also misclassified search/report as an unsupported action. LFM JSON output likewise marked opening the URL unsupported, moved the search/report request into constraints instead of retaining a valid information requirement, and invented a “report only the heading” constraint. LFM native-function arguments were malformed against the production schema and Swift decoding contract: the URL action omitted expectedEffect, and the information object omitted instruction/kind. Both models fail the frozen external oracle; no Swift decoder replay or host execution was attempted. Negative purchase/edit follow-ups remain skipped.
hypothesis: response_format JSON Schema constrains generation without exposing schema to the model; native tool calling injects the schema into the prompt and might better match the model training protocol.

primaryRuntimeDocumentation.section: JSON Schemas → GBNF, note at lines 322–323
primaryRuntimeDocumentation.claim: The pinned docs say JSON Schema constrains model output but is not injected into the prompt, while tool-calling schemas are injected.

comparison.baseline: 01-current-json-schema.json uses production response_format json_schema named browser_goal_contract strict=true.
comparison.candidate: 02-native-function.json uses one interpretGoal native function, description exactly “Return the goal interpretation.”, parameters identical to production schema, strict=true, tool_choice required, parallel_tool_calls false.
comparison.unchanged: Messages, model alias, goal instructions, ordered user JSON, sampler, thinking setting, token budget, and schema parameters were identical; only the interface fields changed.

externalOracle.purpose: Host-side review oracle kept outside every model request.

acceptance: Retain the explicit visit to supplied reference user-url-1 as an openURL action, or represent that visit as a retrieval step within information without obscuring the visit.
Retain searching for Apollo 11, reporting the heading, and identifying the resulting page as the source.
Do not invent constraints, conditions, outcomes, or facts.
There are no other requested outcomes.
Retain the eventual purchase as an action with its condition that the user approves a price below $25; classify the purchase as unsupported in this contract.
Do not replace the purchase with a wait action or invented condition.
Retain opening supplied reference user-url-1 as an openURL action or as a retrieval step within information, without obscuring the requested edit.
Retain replacing the document title with the exact literal Quarterly plan, leaving the document unsaved; classify the edit as unsupported in this contract.
Do not treat opening the document as satisfying the edit or invent conditions.
